name: Panta OEM Diagnostics Expansion 7
usage_note: Curated and paraphrased from publicly archived OEM technical bulletins. Confirm exact VIN, engine family, emissions generation, ambient conditions, calibration and current OEM procedure before repair.

documents.title: PACCAR MX-13 EPA2013 P1490 cold-weather EGR differential-pressure diagnosis
documents.source: NHTSA archived Peterbilt/PACCAR bulletin E178, April 2017
documents.summary: Peterbilt bulletin E178 states that on PACCAR MX-13 EPA2013 engines, moisture can accumulate and freeze at the EGR pressure-difference sensor and trigger P1490, interpreted as EGR stuck open, potentially illuminating the stop-engine lamp. If freeze-frame data shows ambient temperature below 0 C / 32 F when P1490 activated, the bulletin directs technicians to use its extended test procedure before other diagnostics. Diagnostic lesson: ambient conditions and freeze-frame data matter; do not immediately condemn the EGR valve or sensor without checking the cold-weather bulletin path.

documents.title: PACCAR MX EPA13+ aftertreatment diagnosis uses prioritized diagnostic workflow
documents.authority: OEM PACCAR Technical Information Bulletin E198
documents.source: NHTSA archived PACCAR bulletin E198, September 2017
documents.summary: PACCAR bulletin E198 introduced the Diagnostic Assistant for EPA13 and newer MX-11/MX-13 vehicles with aftertreatment problems. PACCAR describes the tool as prioritizing diagnostic steps toward the most likely root cause while capturing the final repair result. TruckFixHub lesson: Panta should emulate this workflow concept—rank likely causes and tests from the best applicable evidence, preserve vehicle/engine applicability, and use confirmed repair outcomes to improve future prioritization rather than presenting a flat list of possible causes.

documents.title: PACCAR MX-11/MX-13 P1710 pressure-sensor plausibility and EGR inspection workflow
documents.authority: OEM Kenworth/Peterbilt PACCAR Service Bulletin E276
documents.source: NHTSA archived PACCAR bulletin E276, February 2021
documents.summary: PACCAR bulletin E276 for applicable MY2019/MY2020 MX-11 and MX-13 engines uses a plausibility-first diagnostic workflow. With key on and engine off, DAVIE is used to compare multiple relative inlet/exhaust pressure signals, which should be near zero, while absolute ambient pressure should agree with local barometric conditions. Implausible signals lead to sensor-tip, port, connector, pin, debris, soot and damage inspection. The workflow then includes EGR-system connection, wiring and sensor inspections. Diagnostic lesson: compare related pressure signals as a system before replacing an individual sensor or EGR component.

documents.title: Cummins cold-weather EGR and air-handling faults — use snapshot temperature and calibration first
documents.authority: OEM Cummins Technical Service Bulletin — Cold Weather Fault Codes
documents.source: NHTSA archived Cummins Cold Weather Fault Codes bulletin, revised 2025
documents.summary: Cummins documents cold-weather faults involving EGR and air-handling components where icing or condensation may occur at ambient temperatures at or below 0 C / 32 F. The bulletin instructs technicians to verify the operating temperature from the fault snapshot in INSITE and compare the ECM calibration code/revision against applicable calibration history. Ice may no longer be visible after the truck enters a warm shop and the fault may become inactive. Where applicable, inspect and clean icing, condensation or residue and follow Cummins cold-climate guidance. Diagnostic lesson: an inactive cold-weather EGR/air-handling fault should not automatically trigger component replacement; preserve snapshot context and verify calibration first.
